candidates.new:
STA stop_y                  \ A kept in stop_y (dead here), not on the stack
    LDA v_ptr
    SEC
base_lo = * + 1
    SBC #0                          \ self-modified: the block's start - 8
header_lo = * + 1
    STA &FFFF,X                     \ self-modified: the header
    LDA v_ptr + 1
base_hi = * + 1
    SBC #0
header_hi = * + 1
    STA &FFFF,X
    LDA stop_y
candidates.summary: mark_part keeps A in stop_y (&C6, renderer scratch dead at this point) instead of PHA/PLA: STA zp + LDA zp = 6 cycles against 3 + 4 = 7 on each of 2.2 calls a pass; +2 bytes.
candidates.equivalence: mark_part's only job beyond the header stores is to hand A back unchanged. PHA/PLA keep it on the stack; STA tmp/LDA tmp keep it in a zero-page byte instead. Register results are identical on every path: A = the entry A (LDA sets N and Z from it as PLA did), X and Y untouched by the replacement, C as the second SBC left it (neither PLA nor LDA zp touches C), V unchanged. The stack is no longer used (S at exit as at entry either way). The only new fact: stop_y is dead across the call. stop_y is written only by draw_column (once per part, before its byte loop reads it); the only readers are that loop's CPY; mark_part has two callers (draw_mover's part two and part three, each followed directly by JSR ren_draw_sprite), no other code in src/ reads or writes the byte during or between them, interrupts do not touch &C0-&CD while the renderer runs (v_ptr = &C4 is live across the whole of put_on in the same way), and it is not in zp_save/restore_game_zp (render_zp.6502 saves only &C0 of the range), so writing it extra cannot change what the logic finds after a render beyond what draw_column's own writes already do.
candidates.relies_on: Page crossings: mark_part2/3 stay at the same addresses (&9A23-&9A29) and the BRA stays inside its page; the body grows by 2 bytes so draw_mover and everything after it in bank 4 slides up 2. Checked on the DEBUG_LIVES bench listing against pc-seed1/pc-right: only two conditional branches change their cross/no-cross status for a +2 slide, both from crossing to not crossing (BEQ in_hazel at &9CFC, 10,707 cycles in the profiles; BEQ gathered at &9EFD, 3,694), so the slide cannot cost there; no other branch moves across a page. Hot indexed table reads that sit after the slide and whose base moves by 2 (straight_sprite_hi/lo &A4E4/&A498, sprite_column_count &A366, ck_* &A3xx-&A4xx, wa_rows_* &A0F5-&A151, raise_cells_* &9D8B/&9D93) could change crossing counts by a few indices either way; the gate measures that. The tail of put_on and the JMP record_live are unchanged.
